deviations: Item 4: CloseLoopCheckpointRequest has no pause_ref, only (run_id, seq, reason), and a continuation does not know the fold's seq. So `fold::close_continued_pause` first calls ClaimLoopCheckpoint with pause_ref `{run_id}:{paused step}` and the request's claim_token, which answers the seq (the claimed fold's bytes are dropped unread), then closes at that seq. The claim also moves the fold off `paused`, so nobody else can claim it. Side effect for the lead: session-core records a CHECKPOINT_RESTORED event for that claim although nothing was restored. If that audit event is unwanted, the clean fix is a session-core close by pause_ref, which touches session-core grpc.rs (s7a-hardening's file), so I did not do it. The close reason `continued_at_stage_1` needed no session-core change.

Item 4 timeouts: the stage-1 claim and close use ROUND_SAVE_TIMEOUT (2 s each), not the 10 s gated timeout, so a hung session-core delays a stage-1 continue by at most 4 s. close_rpc gained a timeout parameter; its other caller passes GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT.

Item 4 gate: the WriterGate for the stage-1 close is built inside fold.rs (close_continued_pause takes zdr, waived and space), not in agent.rs. tests/durable_loop_contract.rs (static proof, not owned by this round) requires exactly one WriterGate literal in agent.rs. I did not edit that file.
Item 5: the getter is `FoldWriter::segment()`, not `segment_no()`: the same contract test forbids `.segment_no` anywhere in agent.rs production code (it is the client-supplied resume field).

Item 3: scrub::scrub_fold now returns `#[must_use] FoldScrub` instead of (); the only production caller is fit. 'Message field' is read as every conversation text field (messages, the open round's assistant text, call ids and names, completed output, error and call_id). Withheld retrieval signatures and call arguments are not counted: a stub in a signature only affects the duplicate-search gate. The existing test loop_fold_saved_bytes_contain_no_seeded_secret was changed: its credential-shaped assistant sentence now yields a tombstone instead of a stub.

Item 2: the log token for a refusal is outcome=refused plus a `cause` field (not_found, denied, unimplemented, key_unavailable) on the save line and on one warn when the writer fails. Append to the 2026-10-18 S6 writer-rules entry (hardening round after adversarial review):

- Open-round folds snapshot `attempted_retrievals` at the START of the round. The phase-1 pre-pass inserts the round's own knowledge_search signatures, so a pre_effect or pause fold that carried the set after it would make an in-place resume that re-runs the pre-pass over the open round reject its own search as a duplicate of itself. The end-of-round fold keeps the final set. Goldens use the real `route|top_k|normalised query` signature.
- Deterministic refusals fail the writer at once. NotFound (run not found), PermissionDenied and Unauthenticated, Unimplemented (a session-core that predates SaveLoopCheckpoint) and FailedPrecondition 'loop checkpoint key unavailable' are `SaveError::Refused` with closed causes not_found, denied, unimplemented and key_unavailable. The writer becomes Failed (fail closed, effects held for the rest of the run, one RPC per run, one content-free warn naming the cause), and the held-back text for a Failed writer says the step could not be started safely in this run and never invites a retry. Reason: retrying a deterministic refusal each round held every effect and told the model 'Try again.' until max_rounds. ResourceExhausted is transient (Unavailable), not a content refusal; InvalidArgument and OutOfRange stay malformed-content refusals.
- A withheld conversation field degrades the fold to a tombstone (reason credential, never resumable). A message, the open round's text, a call's id or name, or a completed outcome that is still credential-shaped after scrubbing used to be replaced by a fixed stub inside a fold that stayed resumable, so a resume would continue on a damaged conversation (the goal, a tool result or a system message replaced) with nothing to say so. Call arguments are still withheld (empty, never rewritten) and keep the fold resumable, because an empty-argument call is never redispatched.
- A stage-1 continuation closes the pause fold it consumed. Right after the approval's consume is won and before the segment dispatches anything, the fold saved under pause_ref `{run_id}:{paused step}` is claimed (to learn its seq; CloseLoopCheckpoint is by seq) and closed with reason `continued_at_stage_1`. Attempted only with the checkpoint switch and effect ledger on and a persistent run; best effort, content-free log tokens, a failure or a disabled store is ignored and never stops the segment. Reason: the paused fold stayed claimable (state paused) while stage 1 ran effects it knew nothing about. Known side effect: the claim records a CHECKPOINT_RESTORED event in session-core although nothing was restored; a close-by-pause_ref in session-core would avoid that.
- Seeding for S7b: FoldWriter::seeded(channel, bearer, run_id, expected_seq, segment_no) and SeqTracker::seeded(expected); every Snapshot reads the writer's segment number (1 for a run's first loop).

S7b obligations created by this round (binding):
(a) An in-place resume must cross-check the effect ledger against the fold and refuse (fall back to stage 1) when the ledger holds actions the fold does not account for. A writer that went Off (StoreOff or NotPersistent) after an earlier successful save leaves a stale resumable fold behind an effect that ran.
(b) An empty step_id call is never dispatched by a resume, whatever the completed list says. A withheld-arguments call (arguments_json empty) is likewise never redispatched.
(c) A fold left active behind a pending approval is not resumable by crash recovery: S8 must require the pause_ref match for approval pauses and must never crash-park a run that has an unconsumed loop approval.
(d) If S7b claims the pause fold in place and then falls back to stage 1, it must not run the stage-1 close (the fold is 'resuming' under its claim); the S7 spec's rule that the fallback does not close the fold stands.

Build ledger amendment to the WS03 S6 entry (hardening round, unit s6-hardening). Done, test-first, no docker, no DB tests: (1) open-round folds snapshot attempted_retrievals at the round start (agent.rs retrievals_at_round_start; goldens now use the real signature hybrid|5|find the contract; new agent tests run the open round through the real retrieval gate for a pre_effect and a pause fold; new golden test in mp-contracts); (2) SaveError::Refused(RefusedBy) for NotFound, PermissionDenied/Unauthenticated, Unimplemented and 'key unavailable': writer Failed at once, one RPC per run, held_for_good_text without 'try again', ResourceExhausted now transient; (3) a withheld conversation field makes the fold a tombstone (reason credential), withheld call arguments stay resumable with empty arguments (scrub_fold returns FoldScrub); (4) a stage-1 continuation claims by pause_ref then closes the pause fold it consumed (reason continued_at_stage_1) before its first effect, best effort, only with switch, ledger and a persistent run, three tests; (5) FoldWriter::seeded, SeqTracker::seeded, Snapshot reads FoldWriter::segment(); (6) agent-level tests for a secret in pre_effect arguments, NotPersistent/Closed/run_ended, the gated call held on a failed pre_effect save, a tombstone save failure, Stale/Closed/StoreOff on the pause save, and mutation proofs for the depth, resumed and waived gates; (7) the posture-matrix test over WriterGate::decide and run_pause_mode is in fold.rs; (8) docker-compose comment corrected, no value changed. Counts: mp-contracts lib 113, golden 10 to 11; execution-core lib 968 to 985; all integration suites unchanged and green. S7b obligations: see the ledger entry (a) ledger cross-check before an in-place resume, (b) empty step_id and empty-argument calls are never dispatched, (c) S8 requires the pause_ref match and never crash-parks a run with an unconsumed loop approval, (d) no stage-1 close after an in-place claim. findings.issue: Items 3 and 4 together leave a resumable fold behind effects that ran. The unit says that when a message field is withheld, "the fold saved is a tombstone". That holds for round and pre_effect folds but not for the pause fold. PauseFold::save maps every error, ContentRefused included, to `Err(_) => PauseSaved::NotSaved` and saves no tombstone. Item 3 makes that refusal much more frequent: it used to be a stub inside a fold that still saved as `paused`. When the pause fold is refused, the stored row stays the earlier ACTIVE, resumable pre_effect fold. The new stage-1 close cannot reach that row: it claims by pause_ref, and claim only matches state paused or parked with that pause_ref, so it answers not_claimable and closes nothing. The stage-1 segment then dispatches effects while a resumable pre_effect fold remains for S8 crash-park to find. Before this round the same path left a stub-damaged `paused` fold, which the new close would have closed.
findings.evidence: fold.rs PauseFold::save: `Err(_) => PauseSaved::NotSaved` (about line 1247). session-core loop_checkpoint.rs claim: `WHERE run_id = $1 AND pause_ref = $4 AND (state IN ('paused','parked') OR ...)`. agent.rs pause site: `completed` = fold_completed(..outcomes..), so a sibling read-only call's credential-shaped output (for example a page containing 'Authorization:') reaches the pause fold, `fit` returns ContentRefused{credential}, and the pre_effect fold saved earlier that round stays active. No test covers a clean pre_effect followed by a content-refused pause.
findings.suggested_fix: In PauseFold::save, handle `SaveError::ContentRefused` like save_round and save_pre_effect do: save a tombstone, best effort, kind round, while the writer is active. Only ContentRefused, so the reconcile ruling that dropped tombstone-on-failed-pause for store failures still holds. Add an agent test: a clean pre_effect fold, then a sibling call whose output is credential-shaped, then the pause. Assert the last stored fold is not resumable. If the lead keeps the reconcile drop for content refusals too, record it explicitly as part of S7b/S8 obligation (c).

findings.issue: close_continued_pause misuses ClaimLoopCheckpoint to learn the seq. The claim has side effects beyond moving the fold off `paused`: (1) session-core decrypts the fold and records a CHECKPOINT_RESTORED event in the run's event log for a restore that never happened, a false audit fact in the run timeline; (2) it leases the fold in state `resuming` under the client-authored claim_token from the /continue body. If the close then fails or times out (both are swallowed), the fold stays `resuming`, becomes claimable again by anyone once the lease lapses, and was decrypted and shipped to execution-core for nothing. So in the failure path the leftover the item set out to remove is still there, and an audit lie has been added.
findings.evidence: loop_checkpoint.rs claim(): `record_event(&mut tx, ..., "CHECKPOINT_RESTORED", ...)` and `SET state = 'resuming', claim_token_hash = $2, claim_expires_at = now() + ...`; the comment there says "Once the lease lapses the pause is claimable again, by anyone". model-gateway sse.rs ContinueRunRequest { approval_id, claim_token } is client-supplied and is passed through as req.resume.claim_token. fold.rs close_continued_pause: a close failure only logs inside close_rpc. The implementer's own deviation 1 acknowledges the event.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a session-core close by (run_id, pause_ref) that touches only a `paused` row with that pause_ref, records no restore event and never decrypts. This needs s7a-hardening's grpc.rs and comment-only proto changes, so the lead should schedule it. Until then, at least record the audit side effect and the failure-path lease in the ledger, and consider skipping the stage-1 close entirely rather than emitting a false CHECKPOINT_RESTORED.

findings.issue: FoldWriter::seeded is a fail-open constructor. It makes an Active writer from nothing but a bearer and skips WriterGate entirely: switch, ledger, zdr, waived, space, depth. Nothing in the type system stops S7b, or anyone else, from building it for a waived or ZDR run. The unit spec mandated this signature, but it is the one writer path the posture-matrix and gate mutation tests do not cover.
findings.evidence: `pub(crate) fn seeded(channel, bearer, run_id, expected_seq, segment_no) -> Self { ... state: if bearer.is_none() { Off(NoBearer) } else { Active } }` with the comment 'The caller (the resume) has already decided that this run may write, so there is no gate'.
findings.suggested_fix: Have seeded take the WriterGate (with resumed=false allowed only for this constructor) or a typed proof issued by the claim, and apply `gate.decide()`. At minimum add an S7b obligation that the seeded writer is built only behind loop_mode_for_persistent and WriterGate, with a mutation test.

findings.issue: The new deterministic Refused class trusts tonic's HTTP-status mapping. A proxy or load balancer answering HTTP 404 during a rollout becomes Code::Unimplemented, and 401/403 become Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied. One such transient answer now fails the writer for the whole run and holds every effectful call until max_rounds, telling the model the step 'will not be run here'. This fails closed, so it is safe, but it is a broad availability cliff with no recovery.
findings.evidence: classify_status: `(Code::NotFound, _) => Refused(NotFound)`, `(Code::PermissionDenied | Code::Unauthenticated, _) => Refused(Denied)`, `(Code::Unimplemented, _) => Refused(Unimplemented)`. Messages are ignored for all three.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the session-core messages where they are fixed ('run not found'), or allow one retry before failing for good for Unimplemented and Denied. Record the choice in the ledger text.

findings.issue: Doc comments in a file this unit owns now contradict the new behaviour. ### WS03 S7a hardening: ListToolActions (2026-10-18)

Status: implemented, DB tests written but awaiting the disposable-Postgres run.

- Authorisation: ListToolActions reads through run_service_grpc::authorize_run_owner, the same helper as GetRun, so a user removed from a run's Space (space_membership_revocations) cannot read that run's ledger. grpc.rs's own authorize_run_owner (no revocation check) was deliberately left alone, so no other RPC changes behaviour.
- Always-on surface closed: the RPC answers the closed `loop_checkpoint_disabled` refusal while SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED is off, decided after the scope and ZDR-human refusals and before any validation or table access. A run whose retention_class is not `persistent` (zdr or zdr_waived) gets the claim path's durable-mutation refusal (FailedPrecondition), because it never keeps a fold. The query also requires retention_class = 'persistent'.
- BINDING S7b RULE: absence is not proof. An action id missing from a ListToolActions answer is UNKNOWN. It may never have been reserved, may be reserved by a concurrent writer that has not committed (one autocommit read, with nothing that fences a live executor), or may be a hidden (zdr) row. An effectful call absent from the read is closed as unknown_outcome and never re-dispatched as `not run, safe to dispatch`; only a row with status not_run (or a completed row with its output) licenses a re-dispatch decision. Written into sessions.proto (comments only), tool_ledger::list_actions and effect::list_actions.
- Client: execution-core effect::list_actions is a thin wrapper over list_actions_with(bearer, run_id, ids, call), which is tested with a closure standing in for the RPC: bearer and run id forwarded, chunks of 64 with every chunk asked, the asked-only check per chunk, unknown status/class/digest is an error, a duplicate answer is an error, an empty list makes no call. Repeated ids are dropped before chunking.
- Not changed: no proto field, message or RPC; the Go bindings need no functional regeneration (only the doc comments of generated files are stale).
- Residual: args_digest is an unkeyed blake3 of canonical arguments, so a reader with session:read in the org could confirm a guess at low-entropy arguments. Accepted as the spec's design; the read is now off by default and refused for non-persistent runs.
